channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Approves Stricter Penalties for Serious Traffic Violations
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan approved a bill on November 28 to toughen penalties for serious traffic violations. The amendments increase fines for speeding and introduce stricter measures against reckless driving and endangering others. New articles will be added to the Criminal Code regarding offenses involving minors.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Strengthens Support for Entrepreneurs and Protects Their Rights
item.description: The Kyrgyz government is enhancing support for entrepreneurs and safeguarding their rights, fostering a stable dialogue between business and authorities. This was stated by Rustam Baltabaev, Executive Director of the Green Energy Development Association of Kyrgyzstan, at a forum on investment. The forum aimed to strengthen cooperation and discuss business challenges.

item.title: Complex Ground Conditions Delay Almaty Thermal Power Plant Construction
item.description: Difficult ground geology and the need to demolish existing structures are hindering the accelerated construction of the second power unit at Almaty's TPP-3. Vice Prime Minister Nurlibek Naliyev visited the site to address these technical issues and coordinate demolition and preparatory works to overcome existing limitations.

item.title: Gas Network Construction Completed in Two Karaganda Neighborhoods, Benefiting Thousands
item.description: The construction of gas distribution networks in the Taugul and Kungay microdistricts of Karaganda has been completed, providing natural gas access to 4,940 private homes. The project included laying 201 km of gas pipelines and installing regulatory points. Social facilities, including schools and kindergartens, will also be connected.

item.title: ING Warns of Budget Deficit Risks Despite Kyrgyzstan's Reported Surplus
item.description: ING analysts estimate Kyrgyzstan's consolidated budget surplus at 2.8% of GDP by September 2026. However, excluding non-tax revenues, the deficit would reach 8.2% of GDP. The financial group also warned of significant risks of overheating the Kyrgyz economy, noting a faster growth in state expenditures than tax revenues.

item.title: Uzbekistan Replaces 30 Russian Military Terms with State Language Equivalents
item.description: Uzbekistan has officially approved a package of 30 new military terms in the state language to replace Russian and borrowed army concepts. Developed by a working group at the Ministry of Defense and reviewed by a Terminology Commission, the new terms include 'ҳамла' for 'attack' and 'дарра' for 'baton'. This initiative aims to expand the use of the state language in the armed forces.

item.title: Talas Declared Cultural Capital of the Turkic World for 2028
item.description: The Permanent Council of the International Organization of Turkic Culture (TURKSOY) has declared Talas, Kyrgyzstan, as the Cultural Capital of the Turkic World for 2028. This decision coincides with the 100th anniversary of the birth of writer Chingiz Aitmatov, whose works are deeply connected to the region.

item.title: Uzbekistan Upgrades Consulate in Mazar-i-Sharif to Consulate General
item.description: Uzbekistan's consulate in Mazar-i-Sharif will be elevated to a Consulate General starting December 1st. This upgrade aims to enhance trade and economic cooperation between Uzbekistan and Afghanistan, and expand opportunities for protecting the interests of citizens and entrepreneurs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Entrepreneurs Urge Swift Reinstatement of Business Ombudsman
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's entrepreneurs are calling for the rapid resumption of the business ombudsman's office. Business associations advocate for transferring the Business and Investment Development Council to the president's purview to address systemic issues. They also propose reviewing and revoking departmental orders affecting businesses.

item.title: Kyrgyz Agroholding Develops Seed, Oil, and Poultry Projects
item.description: Kyrgyz Agroholding is implementing three projects in seed production, vegetable oil processing, and poultry farming. A seed potato storage complex is nearing completion in Naryn region. The company plans to launch domestic vegetable oil brands and produce hatching eggs. Domestic seed potato production has significantly increased.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ombudsman Reports Low Prosecution Rate for Early Marriages
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ombudsman has identified systemic failures in state bodies' handling of early marriage cases. Out of 340 reported instances last year, only 64 resulted in legal action. Commissions for children's affairs are reportedly approving marriage age reductions without thorough verification, often based on pregnancy claims without documentation.

item.title: Two Uzbek Citizens Die in Almaty House Fire
item.description: Two citizens of Uzbekistan died in a house fire in Almaty, Kazakhstan, succumbing to smoke inhalation. The fire occurred in a rented room in a dormitory-style house in the Bostandyk district on November 26. Five people, including a child, perished in the blaze. An investigation into the cause of the fire is underway.

item.title: Snow Leopard Photographed Again in Uzbekistan's Hissar Reserve
item.description: A snow leopard, one of Central Asia's rarest predators, has been captured on a camera trap in Uzbekistan's Hissar State Reserve. This elusive animal, listed in the Red Book of Uzbekistan and under international protection, is believed to number around 80 individuals in the reserve. Uzbekistan participates in international conservation programs for the species.

item.title: Astana Lawyer Sentenced to Two Years for Attempted Bribery
item.description: A lawyer in Astana has been sentenced to two years in prison for attempting to solicit a bribe of 7 million tenge. He promised to ease his client's pre-trial detention by leveraging alleged connections. The client reported the illegal offer, leading to the lawyer's arrest.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Overhauling University Entrance Exams and ORT System
item.description: Kyrgyz lawmakers are debating changes to the country's university admission system, including the Republican Testing (ORT). Proposals include transferring ORT administration to the Ministry of Education and addressing universities that require separate entrance exams. Concerns were raised about ORT preparation becoming a business.

item.title: Uzbekistan Studies China's Economic Growth Strategies for Development
item.description: Uzbekistan is examining China's economic growth factors, including agricultural reforms, special economic zones, pilot projects, poverty reduction, and investment in science and technology. Economist Azizbek Nigmanov analyzed how these approaches are being applied in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Tajik and Russian investigators discuss legal assistance in criminal cases
item.description: Representatives from Tajikistan's Ministry of Internal Affairs Investigative Department and Russia's Investigative Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs held a working meeting in Moscow. They discussed the organization of legal assistance in criminal cases and the practical execution of requests for such assistance. The meeting aimed to strengthen professional ties and enhance international cooperation in law enforcement.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Interior Ministry Addresses Students on Safety and Law Violations
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs has urged students and university administrations to prioritize safety and prevent offenses. Since the start of the academic year, 566 offenses have been suppressed, including violations of migration laws. Police patrols and enhanced security measures are in place in student dormitories.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Audit Chamber conducts first joint audit program with World Bank
item.description: Uzbekistan's Audit Chamber has launched joint audit projects with the World Bank, marking a significant step in its transformation towards international auditing standards. The chamber conducted its first audit of the EduImkon program, implemented with the World Bank, receiving positive evaluations. Future cooperation aims to include the chamber in the list of acceptable auditors for World Bank projects.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan leads Central Asia in food price inflation for plov ingredients
item.description: In October 2026, Kyrgyzstan recorded the highest food price inflation for plov ingredients among three Central Asian countries, with costs rising 12% year-on-year to 850 soms. While plov ingredients are cheaper in Kazakhstan and more expensive in Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan experienced the fastest price growth. Analysts used a six-ingredient plov recipe for comparison.

item.title: Central Asian Activist Investigates Fate of Citizens Captured in Ukraine War
item.description: An activist and political analyst from Kyrgyzstan has been documenting the experiences of Central Asian citizens, primarily from Uzbekistan, captured while fighting for Russia in Ukraine. He has released new videos interviewing these individuals, raising questions about their motivations and the lack of government interest in their fate.

item.title: Uzbekistan Strengthens Penalties for Drunk Driving and Allowing Minors to Drive
item.description: Uzbekistan's Senate has approved amendments to laws increasing penalties for repeat drunk driving offenses, potentially leading to up to two years of imprisonment. Stricter punishments are also introduced for allowing minors to drive, with potential imprisonment up to five years if serious injury or death occurs.

item.title: Former Uzbek State Security Deputy Chief Sentenced to 15 Years
item.description: A military court in Uzbekistan has sentenced former State Security Service (SGB) deputy chief, Lieutenant General Gayratulla Yoziev, to 15 years in prison. Several other former high-ranking SGB officials received sentences ranging from 15 to 17 years. Yoziev was convicted of extortion, illegal detention, and abuse of power.

item.title: Seven Students Killed, Over 100 Injured in Kunar Province Explosion
item.description: An explosion at a house near a middle school in the Andarser area of Kunar Province, Afghanistan, killed seven students and injured over 100 others. The blast occurred in a house where dynamite was stored by miners. Investigations into the cause of the explosion are ongoing.

item.title: Kazakhstan Deputy Prime Minister Inspects Almaty Heat Plant Modernization
item.description: First Deputy Prime Minister Nurlan Nalybaev visited Almaty to review the modernization of Heat Plants 2 and 3. The project for Heat Plant 2's transition to natural gas is 97% complete, with full integration planned by December 25. Heat Plant 3's reconstruction aims to increase its capacity to 543.6 MW.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee Confirms Arrest of Former KTZ Executives
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) confirmed the arrest of former executives from Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ) freight services, including its ex-general director, on corruption charges. They were detained in early November and are currently held under judicial sanction for two months. These arrests coincide with a broader anti-corruption investigation.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Tighten Penalties for Evading Customs Payments
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering stricter penalties for evading customs payments, including criminal prosecution for large sums and repeat offenses. Customs authorities will also gain new powers to investigate illegal fireworks smuggling. These proposed changes, approved by the Senate, aim to address a rise in evasion cases and unpaid duties, which amounted to significant sums in recent years. The amendments will modify the Criminal and Criminal Procedure Codes.

item.title: Uzbek Senate Chair Emphasizes Shared Responsibility for National Future
item.description: Tanzila Narbaeva, Chairperson of the Uzbek Senate, stressed the significant responsibility of the executive, parliament, and local bodies in implementing reforms. She called for a clear review of plans and programs across all sectors to ensure the successful execution of initiatives. Narbaeva urged committee chairs to identify legislative gaps and areas needing on-site study, and to develop proposals for supporting international agreements.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Reputation Starts with Local Leaders' Accountability, Says Artist
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's reputation begins with the accountability of local leaders, according to Kyrgyz People's Artist Ishenbek Chalanov. He emphasizes that leaders should address public issues within their authority without waiting for directives. Chalanov noted that direct presidential meetings revealed discrepancies between official reports and the actual situation on the ground.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Upgrade Consulate in Mazar-i-Sharif to Consulate General
item.description: Effective December 1, 2026, Uzbekistan's Consulate in Mazar-i-Sharif will be reorganized as a Consulate General. This decision aims to boost trade-economic ties, support transport-logistics cooperation, enhance regional connectivity, and improve consular service efficiency. The upgrade is expected to strengthen consular activities and protect the interests of Uzbek citizens and businesses.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Doctor Emphasizes HPV Vaccination and Screening for Cervical Cancer Prevention
item.description: A gynecologist from Bishkek's Family Medicine Center No. 1 highlighted the importance of HPV vaccination and screening for preventing cervical cancer. She stated that the human papillomavirus is a primary cause of cervical cancer, and vaccination is recommended for girls aged 9-13. Regular screening is crucial for early detection.

item.title: Iran and US Continue to Exchange Messages Through Qatar and Pakistan
item.description: Iran's ambassador to Pakistan stated that message exchanges between Tehran and Washington, mediated by Qatar and Pakistan, are ongoing. He mentioned that both intermediary countries propose suggestions, which Iran reviews. The Islamabad agreement from June remains the basis for discussions. Iran warned of alternative actions if attacks resume.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Locals Build Artificial Glaciers to Combat Climate Migration
item.description: Residents in Kyrgyzstan are constructing artificial glaciers to provide year-round water for mountain villages, aiming to reverse depopulation caused by climate change. These structures channel water from streams, which freezes in winter and melts in spring to supply reservoirs, helping locals cultivate land and earn income.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers Criminal Liability for Precursor Chemical Violations
item.description: Uzbekistan may introduce criminal liability for repeated violations of precursor chemical regulations, substances used in drug production. The Senate approved a law to amend criminal and administrative codes. This measure aims to combat clandestine drug labs and protect public health, especially among youth.

item.title: Deccan Gold Mines Delivers First Gold Batch from Solton-Sary to Kyrgyzaltyn
item.description: Indian mining company Deccan Gold Mines, through its subsidiary Avelum Partner, has delivered the first 1.2 kg batch of gold-bearing alloy from the Solton-Sary deposit to Kyrgyzaltyn. The company aims to test the entire precious metal sales cycle, from refining to selling gold to the National Bank of Kyrgyzstan. Deccan Gold expects to produce approximately 180 kg of gold by the end of the current financial year on March 31, 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan Assigns Police Officers to Student Dormitories Amidst Rising Crime
item.description: Kazakhstan has assigned police officers to student dormitories nationwide following a reported 566 offenses since the start of the academic year. Measures include enhanced security and entry controls. This initiative follows recent student deaths at Al-Farabi Kazakh National University, where criminal cases have been initiated. Police suspect hazing may be a factor in one of the fatalities.

item.title: Kazakh Debtor Repays 3.2 Million Tenge Alimony Debt After Prosecution Intervention
item.description: In the Talas district of the Zhambyl region, Kazakhstan, a debtor has repaid 3.2 million Tenge in overdue child support after intervention by the prosecutor's office. The debtor had evaded payments since 2023. A pre-trial investigation was initiated under Article 139 of the Criminal Code. The case was dropped after the debtor confessed, expressed remorse, fully settled the debt, and promised future compliance.

item.title: Former Uzbek Security Official Sentenced to 15 Years for Corruption Charges
item.description: A former deputy head of Uzbekistan's State Security Service, Lieutenant General Gayratulla Yoziyev, has been sentenced to 15 years in prison. A Tashkent-based human rights activist reported that Yoziyev was found guilty of extortion, unlawful detention, and abuse of power. Several other former high-ranking security officials also received prison sentences.

item.title: Russia Explores Cooperation with Tajikistan on Rare Earth Mineral Exploration
item.description: Russia is considering cooperation with Tajikistan to explore the country's mineral resources, with a particular interest in rare earth metals. Rosatom Nedra's First Deputy General Director, Alexey Shemetov, stated that Tajikistan's mineral resources are underexplored and hold significant potential for rare and rare earth metals, which have growing global demand.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sees Significant Increase in Condensed Milk Production
item.description: In Kazakhstan, the production of condensed and concentrated milk and cream has surged by 1.7 times, reaching 6.4 thousand tons in January-October 2026. Overall dairy production remained stable, but butter and cheese output also saw notable increases. Production of traditional drinks like kumys rose, while shubat production nearly halved.
